runtime_boundary: Represents the self-hosted serving engine. Managed services that deploy vLLM on a customer's behalf are separate inference-service boundaries, and the models it serves are not part of this record.
model_management: Models load from Hugging Face repositories or local paths at server start, with adapter and quantization support. Weights are pinned by the launch configuration rather than managed through a runtime model store.
hardware_requirements: Documented execution covers NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and x86, ARM, and PowerPC CPUs, with further accelerators available through a plugin architecture that includes TPU, Gaudi, Spyre, and Ascend targets.
operational_controls: Parallelism strategy, batching, prefix caching, and speculative decoding are configured at launch. The project documents an observability surface for a running server alongside distributed deployment guidance.
strengths: Serving capability is the most complete in the collection, covering continuous batching, chunked prefill, prefix caching, and tensor, pipeline, data, expert, and context parallelism.
Quantization and weight-format coverage spans FP8, MXFP8, NVFP4, INT8, INT4, GPTQ, AWQ, GGUF, and compressed-tensors.
Serves an OpenAI-compatible API alongside an Anthropic Messages API and gRPC, with structured outputs and tool calling.
tradeoffs: The engine targets accelerator-backed server deployment; it is not packaged as a desktop application and has no graphical interface.
Accelerators beyond NVIDIA and AMD depend on plugins whose maturity varies by target.
Model selection is fixed by launch configuration, so changing weights means restarting or running another instance.
license_note: The repository publishes a single Apache-2.0 license file covering the serving engine.
